ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\odot O$ is the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $CD$ is connected. If $AD=3$, $AC=2$, then what is the value of $\cos B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD$ is the diameter of the circle $\odot O$,\\
thus $\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
therefore, by the Pythagorean theorem, $CD=\sqrt{AD^{2}-AC^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
since $\angle B=\angle D$,\\
thus, $\cos B=\cos D=\frac{CD}{AD}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, and the center of the circle is labeled O. A is above the circle, B is on the left side, C is on the right side, and D is on the lower left; line segment AD passes through the center of the circle O, indicating that AD is a diameter; the figure also connects line segments such as AC, BC, CD, etc. Then reason: Because AD is a diameter of the circle, from the fact that the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle, it can be known that ∠ACD=90°. Given AD=3, AC=2, in right triangle ACD, AD is the hypotenuse, therefore CD=sqrt(AD^2-AC^2)=sqrt(3^2-2^2)=sqrt(5). In right triangle ACD, cos∠ADC=CD/AD=sqrt(5)/3. Also because ∠ABC and ∠ADC are both inscribed angles subtended by the same chord AC, ∠B=∠D, that is, ∠ABC=∠ADC. Therefore cos B=sqrt(5)/3.
